title: Shortcut Keys (Windows & Office)
subtitle: Universal Ctrl shortcuts, Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Outlook, Windows-key combos - the time-saver across every Office task

readingSections.title: Universal Shortcuts: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+Z
readingSections.quickSummary: The 7-10 universal shortcuts that work in EVERY Windows app: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo, Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+F find.
content: The 'universal' keyboard shortcuts are the ones that work in (almost) every Windows application - browsers, MS Office, Notepad, File Explorer, even most third-party tools. Memorise these first because they save the most time.

Ctrl+C = COPY the selected text or object to the clipboard. Ctrl+X = CUT (copy + remove). Ctrl+V = PASTE from the clipboard. The clipboard is a temporary storage area in Windows; only one item is stored at a time (unless you use Win+V in Windows 10/11 to open clipboard history).

Ctrl+Z = UNDO the last action. Most apps support multiple undos (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Z...) to walk back through history. Ctrl+Y = REDO - undo the undo. In MS Word, the undo list is famously long (hundreds of actions).

Ctrl+A = SELECT ALL in the current document / window. Ctrl+S = SAVE. Ctrl+P = PRINT (or open the print dialog). Ctrl+F = FIND (open the find/search bar). These four round out the core 8-10 universal shortcuts you should know cold.

Ctrl+N = NEW (new file in Office; new window in browsers; new email in Outlook; new appointment in Calendar - view-dependent). Ctrl+O = OPEN. Ctrl+W = CLOSE (current tab, document, or window). Ctrl+Esc / Win = open the Start menu.

subsections.title: Clipboard history (Windows 10/11)
subsections.content: Win+V opens the Clipboard history panel - shows the last 25 items you've copied. Click any to paste. Pin items to keep them. Without this, copying one item overwrites the previous. Classic workflow: 'Damn, I needed what I copied 5 minutes ago.' Win+V solves it.

subsections.title: Format Painter (Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V)
subsections.content: Ctrl+Shift+C copies FORMATTING (not text) from the selected area. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes that formatting to a new selection. Used to quickly apply the same look to multiple places. Double-click Format Painter to apply to multiple areas. Works in Word, Excel, PowerPoint.

quickRevision: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste. Clipboard = temporary storage.
Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo. Most apps support multiple undos.
Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+F find.
Ctrl+N new (view-dependent), Ctrl+O open, Ctrl+W close, Ctrl+Esc / Win Start menu.
Win+V = clipboard history. Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V = format painter.
tricks: Ctrl+Y in some apps = Redo, in others (MS Word) = Repeat (a different concept). PowerPoint uses Ctrl+Y for Redo; Word uses Ctrl+Y for Repeat - both are valid, the exam accepts either.
Ctrl+Shift+V pastes WITHOUT formatting in some apps (plain-text paste). Test before assuming.

readingSections.title: MS Word Shortcuts: Formatting, Navigation, Editing
readingSections.quickSummary: Ctrl+B/I/U for Bold/Italic/Underline. Ctrl+L/E/R/J for alignment. Ctrl+Enter for page break. F7 for spell check. Ctrl+Shift+E for Track Changes. Ctrl+F for Find. Ctrl+H for Replace.
content: Character formatting: Ctrl+B = Bold. Ctrl+I = Italic. Ctrl+U = Underline. Ctrl+Shift+D = double underline (Word). Ctrl+Shift+W = underline only the words (skip spaces - useful for legal documents). Ctrl+Shift+A = ALL CAPS (toggles between case styles).

Paragraph formatting: Ctrl+L = align Left. Ctrl+E = align cEnter. Ctrl+R = align Right. Ctrl+J = Justify. Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2 / Ctrl+5 = single / double / 1.5 line spacing. Ctrl+M / Ctrl+Shift+M = increase / decrease paragraph indent.
Navigation: Ctrl+Home = top of document. Ctrl+End = bottom. Ctrl+G = Go to page. Ctrl+F = Find. Ctrl+H = Find and Replace. F5 = Go to (page, section, bookmark, comment).

Editing / structure: Ctrl+Enter = page break. Ctrl+Shift+Enter = column break. Ctrl+Backspace = delete previous word. Ctrl+Delete = delete next word. Shift+End = select to end of line. Shift+Home = select to start. Ctrl+Shift+End = select to end of document.

Document management: Ctrl+N = new document. Ctrl+O = open. Ctrl+S = save. Ctrl+P = print. Ctrl+W = close current document. F7 = spell & grammar check. Ctrl+Shift+E = Track Changes on/off. F1 = Word Help.

subsections.title: Text size shortcuts
subsections.content: Ctrl+Shift+> = increase font size. Ctrl+Shift+< = decrease font size. Ctrl+] = grow by 1 point. Ctrl+[ = shrink by 1 point. Ctrl+0 (zero) = reset to 12pt. Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V = Format Painter (copy / paste formatting).

subsections.title: Headings, lists, comments
subsections.content: Ctrl+Alt+1 to Ctrl+Alt+6 = apply Heading 1-6 styles (Word). Ctrl+Alt+0 = Normal style. Ctrl+Shift+L = bullet list. Ctrl+Shift+N = numbered list. Alt+Ctrl+M = new comment. Ctrl+Shift+E = Track Changes on/off.

quickRevision: Bold Ctrl+B, Italic Ctrl+I, Underline Ctrl+U.
Alignment: Ctrl+L Left, Ctrl+E Centre, Ctrl+R Right, Ctrl+J Justify.
Line spacing: Ctrl+1 single, Ctrl+2 double, Ctrl+5 1.5.
Navigation: Ctrl+Home top, Ctrl+End bottom, Ctrl+G go-to page.
Page break Ctrl+Enter, column break Ctrl+Shift+Enter.
Track Changes Ctrl+Shift+E, Spelling F7, Help F1.
tricks: Ctrl+0 (zero, not the letter O) resets font size to 12pt. Easy to mix up.
Ctrl+Shift+> grows font by one PRESET step (12 → 14 → 18 ...). Ctrl+] grows by exactly 1 point each press.
If a question lists 'Ctrl+Shift+B' as Bold -> wrong. Ctrl+Shift+B is something else (in some apps, paste as plain text). Ctrl+B alone is Bold.
patterns: 'Shortcut to insert a page break?' -> Ctrl+Enter.
'Shortcut to turn Track Changes on?' -> Ctrl+Shift+E.

readingSections.title: MS Excel Shortcuts: Cell, Selection, Editing, Formulas
readingSections.quickSummary: Ctrl+Arrow navigates to the edge of data. Ctrl+Space / Shift+Space selects column/row. F2 edits the active cell. Ctrl+; today's date. Ctrl+Shift+L toggles filters. Alt+= auto-SUM. F4 cycles absolute/relative reference.
content: Cell navigation: Ctrl+Arrow key (Up/Down/Left/Right) jumps to the edge of the current data region (e.g. from a cell with data, Ctrl+Down jumps to the last cell with data before an empty row). Ctrl+Home = A1. Ctrl+End = last used cell. Page Up / Page Down = scroll one screen.

Selection: Ctrl+Space = select ENTIRE column. Shift+Space = select ENTIRE row. Shift+Arrow = extend selection by one cell. Ctrl+Shift+Arrow = extend to edge of data. Ctrl+A = select entire data region. Ctrl+Shift+End = select from active cell to last used cell.

Editing: F2 = edit the active cell (move cursor inside). Escape = cancel edit. Enter = confirm and move down. Tab = confirm and move right. Shift+Enter = confirm and move up. Ctrl+Z = undo. Ctrl+Y = redo. Ctrl+D = Fill Down (copies top cell to selected range). Ctrl+R = Fill Right.

Formulas: Alt+= = AutoSUM (sums the column above / row to the left). F4 = cycle cell reference (A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1). Ctrl+; = today's date in the active cell. Ctrl+Shift+; = current time. Ctrl+` = toggle display of formulas / results.

Workbook navigation: Ctrl+Page Down = next sheet. Ctrl+Page Up = previous sheet. Ctrl+G = Go To (cell, named range, comment). Ctrl+F = Find. Ctrl+H = Replace. Ctrl+Shift+L = toggle AutoFilter. F11 = instant chart on a new sheet. Alt+F1 = chart on the current sheet. F2 = rename the current sheet.

subsections.title: Fill series
subsections.content: Type 1, 2 in two cells. Select both. Drag the fill handle (small square at the bottom-right of the selection) and Excel auto-fills the series 3, 4, 5... (or Mon, Tue, Wed... or Jan, Feb...). Or use Home > Fill > Series to control the step.

subsections.title: Cell formatting shortcuts
subsections.content: Ctrl+1 = Format Cells dialog. Ctrl+B/I/U = bold / italic / underline. Ctrl+Shift+$ = Currency format. Ctrl+Shift+% = Percentage format. Ctrl+Shift+! = Number format with comma separator. Ctrl+Shift+# = Date format. Ctrl+Shift+@ = Text format.

quickRevision: Ctrl+Arrow = jump to edge of data region.
Ctrl+Space = column; Shift+Space = row.
F2 = edit cell. Enter confirm + down. Tab confirm + right.
Alt+= = AutoSUM. F4 = cycle A1/$A$1/A$1/$A1.
Ctrl+; = today. Ctrl+Shift+; = time. Ctrl+` = show formulas.
Ctrl+Page Up/Down = next/previous sheet. Ctrl+Shift+L = AutoFilter.
tricks: Ctrl+D copies the top cell of a selection down. Ctrl+R copies leftmost cell right. These are the Fill shortcuts.
F4 cycles reference types in formula edit mode. Without selecting a reference, F4 does nothing useful.
Ctrl+Shift+L toggles AutoFilter on the current data set. Most-asked Excel filter shortcut.
patterns: 'Shortcut to insert today's date in a cell?' -> Ctrl+;.
'Shortcut to go to the last used cell?' -> Ctrl+End.

readingSections.title: PowerPoint & Outlook Shortcuts
readingSections.quickSummary: PowerPoint: Ctrl+M new slide, Ctrl+D duplicate, F5 show. Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+M new email, Ctrl+R reply, Ctrl+F forward, F9 send/receive, Ctrl+Shift+K new task.
content: PowerPoint: Ctrl+M = new slide. Ctrl+D = duplicate selected slide. Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V = copy / paste formatting. F5 = start slide show from beginning. Shift+F5 = from current slide. Esc = end show. B = black screen. W = white screen. Alt+F5 = Presenter View. Ctrl+G = group objects. Ctrl+Shift+G = ungroup.

Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+M = new email from anywhere. Ctrl+R = Reply. Ctrl+F = Forward. Ctrl+Shift+R = Reply All. F9 = Send/Receive (force send / fetch). Ctrl+1 = switch to Mail view. Ctrl+2 = Calendar. Ctrl+3 = Contacts. Ctrl+K = check names in address book.
Outlook calendar: Ctrl+Shift+A = new appointment from anywhere. Ctrl+Shift+Q = new meeting request. Ctrl+Shift+K = new task. Ctrl+G = go to date. Ctrl+1/2/3/4 = day/work week/week/month view.

Universal: Ctrl+Shift+P (insert picture from file) and Ctrl+Shift+V (paste) are useful in every Office app. Ctrl+1 opens Format Cells (Excel) or Format Picture / Format Object (PowerPoint) or Format Text Effects (Word). The Ctrl+1 shortcut is one of the most useful 'tool the exam forgets to ask' shortcuts.

subsections.title: Outlook reading / marking
subsections.content: Ctrl+U = mark the selected message as read (or unread, depending on context). Ctrl+Q = mark as read and move to the next. Ctrl+Shift+A = mark all messages in the current folder as read. F4 = Reply (in older Outlook).

subsections.title: PowerPoint presentation navigation
subsections.content: N or Right arrow / Space / Page Down = next slide. P or Left arrow / Page Up = previous. Number + Enter = jump to slide N (e.g. 5 then Enter). B = black. W = white. . = black (alternate). , = white. F1 = keyboard shortcut overlay.

quickRevision: PowerPoint: Ctrl+M new slide, Ctrl+D duplicate, F5 show, B/W blank screen, Ctrl+G group.
Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+M new email, Ctrl+R reply, Ctrl+F forward, Ctrl+Shift+R reply all, F9 send/receive.
Outlook calendar: Ctrl+Shift+A appointment, Ctrl+Shift+Q meeting, Ctrl+Shift+K task.
Outlook views: Ctrl+1 Mail, Ctrl+2 Calendar, Ctrl+3 Contacts, Ctrl+4 Tasks.
Ctrl+1 = Format dialog (Cells / Picture / Object) in every Office app.
tricks: Ctrl+M in PowerPoint = new slide. Ctrl+M in Mail view in Outlook = new email. Same shortcut, different app.
F5 in PowerPoint = start slideshow. F5 in Excel = Go To (navigate to a named range or cell). Same shortcut, different app.
Ctrl+1 opens Format dialog in EVERY Office app but the contents differ (Cells, Picture, Object, Font, etc.).
patterns: 'PowerPoint: shortcut to add a new slide?' -> Ctrl+M.
'PowerPoint: shortcut to start the slide show from the beginning?' -> F5.
'Outlook: shortcut for new email from anywhere?' -> Ctrl+Shift+M.

readingSections.title: Windows Key Combos (Win+X, Win+L, Win+D, Win+E)
readingSections.quickSummary: Win key combinations for system-level control: Win+E File Explorer, Win+L lock, Win+D show desktop, Win+X power menu, Win+V clipboard, Win+Arrow snap, Win+Shift+S screenshot.
content: The Windows key (Win) is the key with the Microsoft / Windows logo, usually between Ctrl and Alt. Win+X combinations open system features and Windows tools.

Navigation: Win+E = open File Explorer (the file manager). Win+D = Show Desktop (minimise / restore all windows). Win+L = Lock the screen (sign-in screen). Win+M = minimise all windows. Win+Shift+M = restore minimised windows. Win+Tab = open Task View (timeline / virtual desktops).

Snapping and resize: Win+Left / Win+Right = snap the current window to the left or right half of the screen. Win+Up = maximise. Win+Down = minimise / restore. Useful for working with two apps side by side. Win+Home = minimise all windows except the active one (the 'shake to minimise' feature).

Power user: Win+I = Settings app. Win+X = Power user menu (quick access to Device Manager, Disk Management, Task Manager, etc.). Win+L = lock. Win+R = Run dialog (type 'cmd', 'msconfig', 'regedit' for advanced tools). Win+Shift+S = screenshot a region (Windows 10/11 Snip & Sketch).

Virtual desktops (Win+Ctrl+D / Win+Ctrl+Left/Right): create a new virtual desktop, switch between them. Useful for separating 'work' and 'personal' on one machine. Win+V = clipboard history (Windows 10/11).

subsections.title: Screenshot shortcuts (Windows 10/11)
subsections.content: PrtScn (Print Screen) = full screenshot to clipboard. Win+PrtScn = full screenshot saved to Pictures\Screenshots. Alt+PrtScn = screenshot of the ACTIVE window only. Win+Shift+S = region select (Snip & Sketch - rectangle, freeform, window, full screen).

subsections.title: Task Manager
subsections.content: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager directly (skip Ctrl+Alt+Del). Task Manager shows running processes, CPU / memory / disk / network usage, startup programs (Task Manager > Startup tab to disable startup items). The most powerful 'is something slow?' diagnostic tool in Windows.

quickRevision: Win+E = File Explorer. Win+L = Lock. Win+D = Show Desktop.
Win+I = Settings. Win+X = Power user menu.
Win+Left/Right = snap. Win+Up = maximise. Win+Down = minimise/restore.
Win+Shift+S = region screenshot.
Win+V = clipboard history. Win+Ctrl+D = new virtual desktop.
Ctrl+Shift+Esc = Task Manager directly.
tricks: Win+L is the keyboard shortcut you should press EVERY time you walk away from your desk - it locks the screen and protects the laptop.
Win+PrtScn saves the screenshot as a file in Pictures\Screenshots. PrtScn alone puts it on the clipboard (you have to paste it somewhere).
Win+Shift+S is the modern way to take a region screenshot in Windows 10/11 - no need for the old Snipping Tool.
patterns: 'Shortcut to open Task Manager directly?' -> Ctrl+Shift+Esc.
'Shortcut to take a region screenshot?' -> Win+Shift+S.
'Shortcut to snap a window to the left half of the screen?' -> Win+Left.

formulas.title: The 8 Universal Shortcuts (must memorise)

formula.text: C copy, V paste, X cut, Z undo. A select all, S save, P print, F find.

formulas.whenToUse: Any 'which shortcut does X?' MCQ in any app. Universal = works in (almost) every Windows application.
explanation: EDIT: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo.
NAVIGATE / MANAGE: Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+H replace (Office apps).
FILE: Ctrl+N new (view-dependent), Ctrl+O open, Ctrl+W close.
RECOVERY: Ctrl+Z undo (most apps support multiple undos - up to 100 in Office), Ctrl+Y redo.
FORMATTING: Ctrl+B/I/U for Bold/Italic/Underline; Ctrl+L/E/R/J for align Left/Centre/Right/Justify.

example.prompt: Shortcut to copy selected text to the clipboard?
steps: Ctrl+C = copy. Ctrl+X = cut. Ctrl+V = paste. Ctrl+Z = undo.

formulas.memoryTip: C/V/X/Z = the edit shortcuts. A/S/P/F = the navigate/manage shortcuts. The alphabet is the menu.
formulas.commonMistake: Confusing Ctrl+Y (redo) with Ctrl+F (find). Different letters, different actions.

formulas.title: Word Formatting: B/I/U + L/E/R/J

formula.text: B/I/U for character formatting. L/E/R/J for paragraph alignment (Left/cEntre/Right/Justify).

formulas.whenToUse: Any 'shortcut for bold / italic / align' MCQ. The most-tested formatting shortcuts.
explanation: Character: Ctrl+B Bold, Ctrl+I Italic, Ctrl+U Underline. Toggle each (press twice to remove).
Paragraph alignment: Ctrl+L Left, Ctrl+E cEntre (note the British spelling - 'E' for centre), Ctrl+R Right, Ctrl+J Justify (both edges straight).
Line spacing: Ctrl+1 single, Ctrl+2 double, Ctrl+5 1.5.
Font size: Ctrl+] grow 1pt, Ctrl+[ shrink 1pt, Ctrl+Shift+> grow preset, Ctrl+Shift+< shrink preset, Ctrl+0 reset to 12pt.
Page break: Ctrl+Enter (manual page break). Column break: Ctrl+Shift+Enter (newspaper-style columns).
Track Changes: Ctrl+Shift+E. Spelling: F7. Help: F1. Close document: Ctrl+W.

example.prompt: Shortcut to centre the selected paragraph?
steps: L = Left, E = cEntre, R = Right, J = Justify.

formulas.memoryTip: B/I/U for character. L/E/R/J for paragraph. The letters match the action in your head (E for cEntre is the only one that doesn't match perfectly - remember 'English spelling' for British/AU/IN context).
formulas.commonMistake: If the question lists 'Ctrl+Shift+B' as Bold -> wrong. Ctrl+Shift+B is something else (paste as plain text in some apps). Ctrl+B alone is Bold.

formulas.title: Excel Cell-Editing Shortcuts

formula.text: F2 edit cell, Alt+= sum, F4 cycle A1/$A$1, Ctrl+; today, Ctrl+` show formulas.

formulas.whenToUse: Any Excel shortcut MCQ. The five here are the highest-yield.
explanation: F2 = edit the active cell (move cursor inside the cell so you can type at the existing position). Escape = cancel edit. Enter = confirm and move DOWN. Tab = confirm and move RIGHT. Shift+Enter = confirm and move UP. Shift+Tab = LEFT.
Alt+= = AutoSUM. Inserts =SUM(...) and detects the most likely range (column above or row to the left).
F4 = toggle cell reference. In a formula, click a reference and press F4: A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 -> A1. Use $A$1 to lock the column AND row.
Ctrl+; = today's date. Ctrl+Shift+; = current time.
Ctrl+` (backtick / grave accent) toggles the display between formula view and result view. Useful for finding errors.
Ctrl+Space = select entire column. Shift+Space = select entire row. Ctrl+Shift+L = toggle AutoFilter.

example.prompt: Shortcut to insert the current date in a cell:

formulas.memoryTip: Ctrl+; = the only date shortcut worth memorising. Semicolon because it's near M on QWERTY (date has M in it - month).
formulas.commonMistake: Ctrl+' (apostrophe, not semicolon) does something different - it enters the value from the cell ABOVE.

formulas.title: PowerPoint & Outlook Top Shortcuts

formula.text: PowerPoint: Ctrl+M new slide, F5 start show. Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+M new email, F9 send/receive.

formulas.whenToUse: Any PowerPoint or Outlook shortcut MCQ. The two apps share the F5 key (different meanings) and have distinctive shortcuts.
explanation: PowerPoint: Ctrl+M = new slide (after the currently selected one). Ctrl+D = duplicate the selected slide. F5 = start the slide show from the beginning. Shift+F5 = from the current slide. Esc = end. B = black screen. W = white screen.
Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+M = new email from anywhere in Outlook. Ctrl+R = reply. Ctrl+F = forward. Ctrl+Shift+R = reply all. F9 = Send / Receive (force Outlook to sync with the server).
Outlook calendar: Ctrl+Shift+A = new appointment. Ctrl+Shift+Q = new meeting request. Ctrl+Shift+K = new task.
Outlook navigation: Ctrl+1 = Mail, Ctrl+2 = Calendar, Ctrl+3 = People (Contacts), Ctrl+4 = Tasks. Same for the 'New' group: Ctrl+Shift+M (email), A (appointment), Q (meeting), K (task), C (contact).
F5 means different things: PowerPoint = start show. Excel = Go To. Word = Go To (Browsing mode). Context-dependent shortcuts are the exam trap.

example.prompt: Shortcut to add a new slide in PowerPoint:
steps: Ctrl+M = new slide. Ctrl+D = duplicate slide.

formulas.memoryTip: PowerPoint Ctrl shortcuts start with Ctrl+M (sli**M**). Outlook Ctrl+Shift shortcuts are 'from anywhere': Ctrl+Shift+M (e**M**ail), Ctrl+Shift+A (**A**ppointment), Ctrl+Shift+Q (meeting re**Q**uest), Ctrl+Shift+K (tas**K**).
formulas.commonMistake: Ctrl+M in Mail view of Outlook = new email. Ctrl+M in Calendar view = new appointment. View-dependent - the same trap as Ctrl+N.

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to paste the clipboard contents:
s: Ctrl+V = paste. (Ctrl+C/X/P do different things.)

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to undo the last action:
s: Ctrl+Z = undo. Ctrl+Y = redo (in most apps).

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to redo the last undone action (in most Office apps):
s: Ctrl+Y = redo. Ctrl+Z = undo. (In MS Word Ctrl+Y means 'Repeat' but most apps treat it as redo.)

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to select ALL in a document:
s: Ctrl+A = select all. Ctrl+S = save. Ctrl+L = left-align (in Word/Outlook).

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to save the current document:
s: Ctrl+S = save. Ctrl+D = bookmark (browser) or duplicate (PowerPoint). Ctrl+W = close.

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to open the Print dialog:

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to open the Find bar:

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to CUT selected text (copy + delete):
s: Ctrl+X = cut. Ctrl+C = copy. Ctrl+D = bookmark / duplicate.

universal-eight.q: Shortcut to close the current window / document / tab:
s: Ctrl+W = close the current document or tab. Alt+F4 = close the entire application. Ctrl+Q is 'quit' in some apps (rare).

word-biu.q: Shortcut to apply Bold formatting to selected text:

Ctrl+I = Italic.
Ctrl+U = Underline.

word-biu.q: Shortcut to align the selected paragraph to the LEFT:
s: L = Left. E = cEntre. R = Right. J = Justify.

word-biu.q: Shortcut to align the selected paragraph to the CENTRE:
s: E = cEntre (British spelling).

word-biu.q: Shortcut to JUSTIFY the selected paragraph (both edges straight):
s: J = Justify. Aligns both left and right edges.

word-biu.q: Shortcut to insert a manual page break in Word:

word-biu.q: Shortcut to apply single line spacing to a paragraph:

word-biu.q: Shortcut to apply double line spacing:

word-biu.q: Shortcut to toggle Track Changes on/off in Word:

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to edit the active cell (move cursor inside):

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to apply AutoSUM in a cell:

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to cycle cell reference types (A1 / $A$1 / A$1 / $A1) in formula edit:
s: F4 cycles: A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 -> A1. Works in formula edit mode.

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to select the ENTIRE COLUMN of the active cell:

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to select the ENTIRE ROW of the active cell:

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to copy a formula from the cell above (Fill Down):

excel-keys.q: Shortcut to move to the next worksheet in the workbook:
s: Ctrl+Page Down = next sheet. Ctrl+Page Up = previous sheet.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Shortcut to add a NEW SLIDE in PowerPoint:
s: Ctrl+M = new slide. (Ctrl+N = new presentation - new file.)

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Shortcut to duplicate the selected slide in PowerPoint:
s: Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide (and selected objects in any Office app).

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Shortcut to start the slide show FROM THE BEGINNING:
s: F5 = from beginning. Shift+F5 = from current slide. Alt+F5 = Presenter View.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Shortcut to end a running slide show:
s: Esc ends the slide show and returns to editing.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: During a slide show, B gives you:
s: B = black screen. W = white screen. Esc = end.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Outlook: shortcut to create a new email FROM ANYWHERE in Outlook:
s: Ctrl+Shift+M = new email from any view. (Ctrl+M in Mail view = new email; in Calendar = new appointment - view-dependent.)

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Outlook: shortcut to REPLY to the sender of the selected message:
s: Ctrl+R = Reply. Ctrl+F = Forward. Ctrl+Shift+R = Reply All.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Outlook: shortcut to force Send / Receive (sync with server):
s: F9 = Send / Receive All. Forces Outlook to check for new mail and send queued mail.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Outlook: shortcut to create a new meeting request (from anywhere):
s: Ctrl+Shift+Q = new meeting request. Ctrl+Shift+A = new appointment. Ctrl+M = view-dependent.

powerpoint-outlook-keys.q: Outlook: shortcut to create a new TASK (from anywhere):
s: Ctrl+Shift+K = new task. (K for tasK.)

mcqs.q: Universal shortcut to COPY selected text or an object:
exp: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo.

mcqs.q: Universal shortcut to PASTE from the clipboard:
exp: Ctrl+V = paste. Ctrl+P = print.

mcqs.q: Universal shortcut to UNDO the last action:
exp: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo (in most apps).

mcqs.q: Universal shortcut to SELECT ALL in the current document / window:
exp: Ctrl+A select all. Ctrl+S save. Ctrl+L left-align. Ctrl+N new.

mcqs.q: Shortcut to SAVE the current file in any Windows app:
exp: Ctrl+S = save. Ctrl+W = close. Ctrl+D = bookmark / duplicate. Ctrl+Q = quit (some apps).

mcqs.q: Shortcut to open the PRINT dialog in any Windows app:
exp: Ctrl+P opens the print dialog. Ctrl+Shift+P in some apps (e.g. Word) toggles superscript.

mcqs.q: Shortcut to open the FIND bar in any Windows app:
exp: Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+H find and replace, Ctrl+G go to, Ctrl+R reload.

mcqs.q: Shortcut to open the Windows Clipboard History (Windows 10/11):
exp: Win+V opens Clipboard History (up to 25 recent copies, with pin option).

mcqs.q: Format Painter copies:
opts: Text formatting (font, size, colour) without the text
exp: Format Painter = copy formatting (not text). Ctrl+Shift+C copies; Ctrl+Shift+V applies.

mcqs.q: Shortcut to open the Start menu from the keyboard:
exp: Ctrl+Esc or the Win key opens the Start menu.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to apply BOLD formatting:
exp: Ctrl+B = Bold. (Ctrl+Shift+B is paste as plain text in some apps - not Bold.)

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to apply ITALIC:
exp: Ctrl+I = Italic.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to apply UNDERLINE:
exp: Ctrl+U = Underline.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to JUSTIFY the selected paragraph (both edges straight):
exp: L=Left, E=cEntre, R=Right, J=Justify.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to insert a manual page break:
exp: Ctrl+Enter = page break. Ctrl+Shift+Enter = column break.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to toggle Track Changes on/off:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+E = Track Changes. F7 = spell check.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to start a Spelling & Grammar check:
exp: F7 = Spelling & Grammar. (F1 = Help, F5 = Go To, F12 = Save As.)

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to open the Find and Replace dialog:
exp: Ctrl+H = Find and Replace. Ctrl+F = Find only.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to go to the BEGINNING of a document:
exp: Ctrl+Home = top of document. Ctrl+End = bottom.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to apply single line spacing:
exp: Ctrl+1 = single. Ctrl+2 = double. Ctrl+5 = 1.5 lines. Ctrl+0 (zero) = 12pt font (different meaning).

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to enter the edit mode for the active cell:
exp: F2 = edit. F4 = cycle reference. F7 = spell check. F11 = new chart on a sheet.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to insert the CURRENT DATE in a cell:
exp: Ctrl+; (semicolon) = today. Ctrl+Shift+; = time.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to apply AutoSUM to the selected cells:
exp: Alt+= = AutoSUM.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to cycle cell reference types (A1 <-> $A$1) in a formula:
exp: F4 cycles: A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 -> A1. Works in formula edit mode.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to select the ENTIRE COLUMN of the active cell:
exp: Ctrl+Space = column. Shift+Space = row.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to toggle AutoFilter on the active data range:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+L = toggle AutoFilter.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to jump to the LAST USED cell in the worksheet:
exp: Ctrl+End = last used cell. Ctrl+Home = A1.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to copy the formula from the cell above (Fill Down):
exp: Ctrl+D = Fill Down. Ctrl+R = Fill Right.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to move to the NEXT worksheet in the workbook:
exp: Ctrl+Page Down = next sheet. Ctrl+Page Up = previous sheet.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to open the Format Cells dialog:
exp: Ctrl+1 = Format Cells (universal Office shortcut for the Format dialog of whatever is selected).

mcqs.q: PowerPoint: shortcut to add a new slide:
exp: Ctrl+M = new slide. Ctrl+N = new presentation (new file).

mcqs.q: PowerPoint: shortcut to duplicate the selected slide:
exp: Ctrl+D = duplicate slide.

mcqs.q: PowerPoint: shortcut to start the slide show FROM THE BEGINNING:
exp: F5 = from beginning. Shift+F5 = from current slide.

mcqs.q: PowerPoint: shortcut to end a running slide show:
exp: Esc ends the slide show.

mcqs.q: During a PowerPoint slide show, B gives you:
exp: B = black screen. W = white. Esc = end. Space = next.

mcqs.q: Outlook: shortcut to create a new email FROM ANYWHERE in Outlook:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+M = new email from any view. (Ctrl+M is view-dependent.)

mcqs.q: Outlook: shortcut to REPLY to the sender of the selected message:
exp: Ctrl+R = Reply. Ctrl+F = Forward. Ctrl+Shift+R = Reply All.

mcqs.q: Outlook: shortcut to FORWARD the selected message:
exp: Ctrl+F = Forward. Ctrl+R = Reply. Ctrl+Shift+R = Reply All.

mcqs.q: Outlook: shortcut to force Send / Receive (sync with server):
exp: F9 = Send / Receive All. F5 = Go To in Outlook (not slide show).

mcqs.q: Outlook: shortcut to create a new meeting request FROM ANYWHERE:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+Q = new meeting. Ctrl+Shift+A = new appointment. Ctrl+Shift+K = new task.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to open FILE EXPLORER:
exp: Win+E = File Explorer. Win+F = Search (older Windows). Win+L = Lock. Win+X = Power user menu.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to LOCK the screen:
exp: Win+L = Lock. Press it every time you walk away from the desk.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to show the DESKTOP (minimise all windows):
exp: Win+D = Show Desktop (toggles). Win+M = minimise all. Win+Tab = Task View.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to take a REGION screenshot (Snip & Sketch):
exp: Win+Shift+S = region select (rectangle, freeform, window, full screen).

mcqs.q: Shortcut to open TASK MANAGER directly (no Ctrl+Alt+Del menu):
exp: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager directly. Alt+F4 closes the active window.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to open the SETTINGS app:
exp: Win+I = Settings. Win+S = Search. Win+X = Power user menu. Win+P = Project (display).

mcqs.q: Shortcut to snap the active window to the LEFT half of the screen:
exp: Win+Left snaps left, Win+Right snaps right. Alt+Left is browser back.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to open the Power user menu (Device Manager, Task Manager, etc.):
exp: Win+X = Power user menu. Quick access to Device Manager, Disk Management, Task Manager, Settings, etc.

mcqs.q: Windows shortcut to create a new virtual desktop:
exp: Win+Ctrl+D = new virtual desktop. Win+Ctrl+Left/Right = switch between them. Win+Ctrl+F4 = close current.

mcqs.q: Windows key shortcut to open the Run dialog (cmd, msconfig, regedit):
exp: Win+R = Run dialog. Type 'cmd', 'msconfig', 'regedit', 'powershell' for advanced tools.

mcqs.q: Format Painter shortcut (copy formatting):
exp: Ctrl+Shift+C copies formatting. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes formatting.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to insert the CURRENT TIME in a cell:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+; = current time. Ctrl+; = today's date.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to align the selected paragraph to the RIGHT:
exp: R = Right. L = Left. E = cEntre. J = Justify.

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to apply 1.5 line spacing:
exp: Ctrl+5 = 1.5 line spacing. (Ctrl+1 = single, Ctrl+2 = double.)

mcqs.q: MS Word: shortcut to go to the END of a document:
exp: Ctrl+End = bottom of document. Ctrl+Home = top.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to select the entire ROW of the active cell:
exp: Shift+Space = row. Ctrl+Space = column.

mcqs.q: MS Excel: shortcut to Fill RIGHT (copy left cell across selection):
exp: Ctrl+R = Fill Right. Ctrl+D = Fill Down.

mcqs.q: Outlook: shortcut to REPLY ALL to a message:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+R = Reply All. Ctrl+R = Reply (just to sender).

mcqs.q: PowerPoint: shortcut to start the slide show from the CURRENT slide:
exp: Shift+F5 = from current slide. F5 = from beginning.

mcqs.q: Shortcut to open the Windows Start menu (universal):
exp: Ctrl+Esc or the Win key opens the Start menu. Ctrl+Shift+Esc = Task Manager. Alt+Tab = switch apps. F1 = Help.
